findings.note: TRAP (state-migration): the naive fix — reject any backup that lacks a pool/store-generation stamp — would reject every backup THIS build has already written, because the exporter still emits version 1 with no stamp. The exporter has to start stamping (pool version + epoch + daily-store version) before the importer can enforce it, and stamp-less files need an explicit degraded path (import the wins map, which is pool-independent, and either drop or clearly warn about the daily map). Two supporting facts: (a) DailyStore already treats a pre-v3 day map as poison and stashes it rather than loading it, so the import path is the only remaining door; (b) TierResult gained `flawless`/`onTime` in the same commit and both decodeIfPresent-default to false, so a legacy file also cannot be told apart from a current one by shape. Aggravating: the merge is instant and irreversible (see ux/WF-11:import-has-no-confirm-or-undo).

findings.claim: The Auto-play pill is presented as a setting but is an immediate, unconfirmed, un-undoable-in-one-tap game action: tapping it mid-game instantly played 2 cards and advanced the move counter 92 -> 94 on a scored daily run. Nothing on the pill, and no confirm, warns that flipping a preference will spend moves against a move-count objective (day 29's silver is 'four Kings within your first 9 moves').

repro: restore any scored daily board with Auto-play: Off and at least one safely-homeable card exposed (day-29 save above, Moves 92)
tap the Auto-play pill (337,135) once
the label flips to On AND the board plays itself: Moves 92 -> 94 with no card ever touched

findings.note: Deliberately NOT a duplicate of bug/WF-4:autoplay-denies-daily-gold: this survives that fix. Even a perfectly direction-safe autoplay still spends real moves the instant a preference is toggled, and Causeway scores move counts (par, 'within your first N moves' objectives, Wins best-moves). Related in family to the open ux/WF-3:board-reset-pills-no-confirm. Cheap options: only apply the new setting from the next player move, or make the pill's first firing on an in-progress game confirm. TRAP: the moves it adds are recorded in the scored stream, so any change here changes recorded results.

findings.claim: The Daily day-card prints the deal number comma-grouped ("Deal #850,804") while the board pill and every Wins surface print the same number ungrouped ("Deal #551879", chip "551879") — the two screens disagree on the identifier a user needs to match, and a user cannot tell whether "Deal #551,879" and "551879" are the same deal. DailyView.swift:181 uses Text("Deal #\(c.seed)"), which interpolates through LocalizedStringKey and auto-groups the digits; it bypasses DealFormat.seed(), the ungrouped formatter added for exactly this bug in WinsView.

repro: launch
tap Daily (270,172)
swipe (200,750)->(200,150) x3 to reach the calendar
swipe (200,340)->(200,700) to scroll the day card into view
read the card's right-hand deal label: 'Deal #691,039'
dismiss the sheet, read the board's Deal # pill and the Wins chips: ungrouped ('Deal #551879' / '551879')

findings.note: One-line fix: Text("Deal #" + DealFormat.seed(c.seed)). Observed on all 7 day cards read this pass (Aug 1-7).

findings.claim: In Wins > 'Play a deal', a number above 1,000,000 leaves Play greyed out with no message and no other feedback — and because the only statement of the legal range is the field's placeholder, which the typed text has replaced, nothing on screen tells the user what is wrong or what to change.

repro: launch
tap Wins (338,172)
tap the 'Play a deal' field (164,186)
observe: field reads 02000000, Play is disabled, no error text, placeholder hint gone

findings.note: Enforcing the bound is right (do not go back to clamping silently); what is missing is a one-line reason under the field, e.g. 'Deal numbers go up to 1,000,000'. TESTCASES TC-9.3 still says 'clamped 1-1,000,000' - the doc, not the app, is stale there.

findings.claim: The solve clock keeps ticking while the app's OWN auto-raised 'Ready to finish' modal blocks play, so a recorded best time silently absorbs however long the user takes to answer a prompt they never asked for (measured: Time advanced 1:35 -> 1:39 across 3.5 s in which the counter was the only pixel on screen that changed). Previously filed against user-opened sheets (Daily/Wins/How to play) in the 342e3c0 loop and never resolved; this is the sharper, app-initiated instance.

repro: node .qa-loop/tools/make_save.mjs --day 20 --tier flawless | python3 .qa-loop/tools/inject_save.py <udid>
xcrun simctl launch <udid> com.whimsicaldistractions.Causeway
the board restores and the app itself raises the modal 'Ready to finish - Every remaining card can go home. Send them all now?' (Not yet / Finish)
do not answer it; film the screen (xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot at ~4 fps)
the Time counter increments once per second for as long as the modal is up, while every other pixel of the screen is byte-identical

findings.note: TRAP: the obvious fix (pause GameClock while any sheet/alert is presented) turns every sheet into a free pause button and corrupts recorded best times in the other direction - a player could stop the clock indefinitely by opening How to play. Any fix must distinguish app-initiated modality (this prompt) from user-initiated sheets, or leave the clock alone and instead not raise the prompt unbidden. Reuses the id filed in the 342e3c0 archive loop (routing proposal, still open there); no re-decision by a human has happened since.
